newsitem.title: USA: Rexworks to sell assets, rest of company.
newsitem.headline: Rexworks to sell assets, rest of company.

text.p: Struggling with falling sales and growing losses, Rexworks Inc. said Monday it agreed to sell off parts of its compactor and grinder business and then to sell the remains of the company in a separate transaction.

Rexworks, based in Milwaukee, said it agreed to sell assets in its compactor and grinder business to CMI Corp., a maker of road building and construction equipment. Terms of the sale to CMI, based in Oklahoma City, were not disclosed.
CMI said the two product lines it plans to acquire had $30 million in sales in the latest fiscal year.
Rexworks, which also makes concrete mixers, also said it agreed to sell its outstanding common stock to Giuffre Bros. Cranes Inc. of Milwaukee.
Net proceeds from the two transactions were expected to be $5 to $5.25 a share, Rexworks said. That would amount to about $9.5 million based on its shares outstanding.
Proceeds would be distributed to shareholders, it said.
The sales are subject to approval by regulators and shareholders. Rexworks said it expects the deals to close about Nov. 30.
Rexworks stock fell 12.5 cents to $4.375 in late morning trading on Nasdaq. CMI rose 6 cents to $5.31 in composite trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
